title: TL-CGAN: How Transfer Learning Conditional GAN Makes Robustness of Electrocardiogram (ECG) Signals Against Adversarial Attacks
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) classifiers deployed in clinical decision-support systems are vulnerable to small, targeted adversarial perturbations that can flip a prediction without any visible distortion to the signal. We propose TL-CGAN, a transfer-learning framework built on conditional generative adversarial networks, that fine-tunes a pretrained ECG classifier against adversarially perturbed inputs generated by a conditional generator. Unlike standard adversarial training, the conditional generator is trained jointly with the discriminator to produce realistic, class-consistent perturbations, which we show yields a more sample-efficient robustness gain than gradient-based augmentation alone. Across FGSM and PGD attack budgets, TL-CGAN preserves clean-signal accuracy within one point of the unmodified baseline while substantially closing the accuracy gap under attack, indicating the approach is a practical route to hardening ECG classifiers for downstream clinical use without retraining from scratch.

title: Deep Neural Networks Approach Towards Histopathological Skin Cancer Segmentation
abstract: Accurate delineation of malignant tissue in histopathological whole-slide images is a prerequisite for reliable computer-assisted skin cancer diagnosis, but manual annotation is slow and subject to inter-rater variability. We present a deep neural network segmentation pipeline, developed with a multi-institution research team, that localizes malignant regions in histopathological skin cancer slides. The approach combines a convolutional encoder-decoder architecture with domain-specific pre-processing to handle the color and staining variability typical of multi-site histopathology datasets. Preliminary results on held-out slides show segmentation masks that closely track expert annotations, and the collaboration is ongoing to extend the dataset and validate the pipeline across additional clinical sites.
